item: three failures on main fixed and 48 test files that read a clock moved to orders, observed handshakes, CPU clocks and the numbers the code asked for
summary: Test-only: src/ and scripts/ are unchanged. Three failures seen on main are fixed, then the same fragility is swept: 48 test files changed (172 tests touched, 2 new), 59 more read and left alone, 3 held out (belonging to other changes). (1) test_write_gate_breakdown: a session's commit bucket is held to the clock around its own commit (held <= took + slack) instead of a fixed bound. (2) test_holder_state: the watchdog-loop simulation records only its own thread's calls (the process's own watchdog woke inside the 50 ms window and was counted as a fourth tick, 1.68 s); a stranger test calls on purpose and fails without the pinning. (3) test_scheduler_runner continuous-loop test: pass two waited behind pass one's real tail (whole-process gc.collect, WAL checkpoint, custody read, off-peak maintenance), not a missing throttle; tests/wallclock_helpers.quiet_pass_tail stubs the tail and the wait is a 20 s guard (a 12 s slowed tail: old test red at 6 s, new green at 25 s, tail stubs removed red at 25 s). THREE FAMILIES, KEPT SEPARATE. A COUNT AFTER A SLEEP, 15 files (a positive count or state after a fixed wait on a running thread; the fix waits for the thing asserted, observed): test_scheduler_runner, test_scheduler and test_scheduler_pause_resume (tail stubbed; stop joins and last_result awaited; injection: stop answered beyond its 10 s join), test_continuous_collection (5 s floor and 2 s deadline to the guard; mutant continuous mode does not continue: red), test_import_queue (mutant stop leaves queued items skipped: red), test_jobs_arbitration and test_osm_jobs (counted polls to wait_until; mutants dumps/osm reorder reversed: red), test_pool_reserve (mutant gate owner queues for a slot: red), test_encrypt_all_write_gate (mutant encrypt_all does not take the gate: red), test_parallel_collect_guardrails (fetches held until the switch trips; mutant fetch path ignores the kill switch: red), test_storage_events (attempts in one second to gap floors 0.13/0.23/0.43 s, 3 s defaults and one explicit 3.0 s to the guard, held parties 60 s with release in finally; mutants retry never backs off, write and first read under the journal lock, _wait_out ignores a reset or its deadline: red), test_rollup_build_streaming (mutants warns on a moving build, never warns of no progress: red; its tests skip on the core profile, so its results are the columnar profile's, duckdb 2.0.0), test_lock_live_reading and test_exit_evidence (the reading awaited; no src mutant, the assertions are unchanged), test_session_hwm_light (mutant reads /proc first: red). THROUGH-TIME, 26 files (an elapsed time held to an UPPER bound; the fix asserts an order, uses a CPU or stepped clock, or reads the number the code asked for): test_custody_late_count_read (mutants encrypted open unbounded, 60 s statement bound: red), test_database_damage (mutants M1-M4: red; record join 5 s for RECORD_WAIT_S and x10: red), test_debug_bundle_hardening (member budget 5 s plus a held member; mutants member waited for, join waits for ever: red), test_discovery_busy_snapshot (variant in which the busy handler is consulted: red), test_encrypt_owns_the_machine (mutant quiescence ignores its deadline: red), test_field_round_defects (mutant queueing waits for a drain: red), test_furniture_stubs, test_markup_anchored_subs and test_markup_strip_linear (CPU clock; mutants that restore a quadratic pass or the retired implementation: red; two first mutants that did not restore the defect stayed green and were replaced), test_handlers_off_the_event_loop (variant with the slow handler on the loop: red), test_heavy_tail_serialisation (mutants lone consumer waits, unbounded wait, wait widened to 5 s: red), test_import_lifecycle_stages (mutant drain on the startup path: red), test_kernel_evidence (mutant read inline: red), test_memory_guard (mutants wind-down blocks, pause wait not interruptible: red), test_plan_cache (mutants stale preview waits, first wait unbounded, first wait 2 s: red), test_release_run (mutants wait ends at its first timeout, pipes unread, collect-now ignored: red), test_restore_swap_locked_files (stepped clock; mutants every OSError retried, keeps waiting after the lock clears, one budget per side file: red), test_shutdown_wal (mutant step inherits the 30 s busy timeout: red), test_storage_guard (stepped clock and read numbers; mutants pause wait not interruptible, stop waits for ever, no join, a full budget per join, stop deadline widened, wait_if_engaged bound widened to 2 s or a poll longer than the time left: red), test_unlock_recovery_progress (mutant neither site zeroes the busy timeout: red; one site alone stays green because the other covers it), test_wiki_lane_history (held <= the span timed around the calls; mutant release charges any thread: red), test_write_gate_breakdown (mutants commit re-opens, statement-end missing, every statement an INSERT, after_commit never closes: red), test_write_gate_holder (mutants hygiene checkpoint waits for the holder, bounded acquire waits 3 s: red; a tenth of the bound stays green, the lower bound lives in the next file), test_write_gate_lost_wakeup (mutants bounded acquire sleeps a whole step, waits 3 s, gives up at a tenth: red), test_swap_barrier (mutants gives up at once, any should_stop returns early, stop ignored: red), test_extract_lock (mutant blank page refused inside the lock: red). FIXED WAIT ON A THREAD, 6 files (a sleep or join to let it get there, then a positive assumption; the fix makes the thread say it is there): test_heavy_guard (mutant cap runs the excess: red), test_heavy_integrity_sweep and test_heavy_paused_wal (the follower observed parked on its flight; mutant no single-flight: red; follower starved 0.6 s: green), test_repair (writer lock observed; mutant busy checkpoint read as a fold: red), test_pin_report_pin (a SQL function that signals and holds; the checkpoint lock seen through a probe; mutant statement ranks last: red), test_holder_state (above). A RATE CLAIM, 1 file: test_wal_starvation_soak (the byte check can fail for a CPU-starved writer: skips with the writer's rate when it could have failed and did not; a synthetic round pins both sides). LEFT ALONE, READ (59 files): an elapsed-time LOWER bound; a negative or blocking assertion after a fixed head start (a late thread weakens it, never reds it); a bound that is not time (counts, widths, byte sizes); a wall-clock upper bound of 30 s or more on a path that takes milliseconds or seconds; a CPU figure; the file list is in the shipped log fragment. HELD OUT: test_backup_snapshot, test_figures_cold_start, test_launcher_records_race, none of which carried the three failures. EVIDENCE on the final tree (4 cores): whole files plain, core 1717 passed 98 skipped, columnar 1815 passed; mild freeze (about 60 % frozen) 96 runs 0 red; clock jump of 8 s at the 2nd to 5th monotonic call 192 runs, the only red a first version of the _wait_out test (fixed, 28 runs 0 red), whole files 192 runs red only in nine test_storage_events tests that feed time.monotonic() - 99_999.999 into the code (31 reds on main's file under the same jump); burners (12 busy loops and 2 fsync hammers, load average 15.75 on 4 cores) 144 runs in 4 min 49 s 0 red, and the seven files of the last commit x 8 reps 56 runs 0 red. LIMITS: the harsh freeze stretches every requested sleep to a freeze cycle, so a sleep-bound test goes red under it with 0.02 s of CPU; a stuck party that outlasts a 20 s guard tells a hang from a wait but not a slow call from a fast one where the code passes no number to read; the soak skips on a starved runner instead of asserting. The runner that failed was not observed; the mechanisms reproduced are the signatures, not a measurement of it.
